# Glyphs that are still drawn as text in the files the icons wave owns.
#
# Format: <path>:<line>  # <reason>   (two spaces before the '#')
# An entry without a reason fails the test, and so does an entry that no
# longer matches anything (tests/test_icons.py) -- an allow-list that
# outlives its offender hides the next one.
#
# Two families, two different reasons. Neither is "we forgot".
#
# ── 1. The ○ / ● / ✓ completion toggle ──────────────────────────────────
# Every card in the app carries the same three-state check button, and the
# canonical one -- TaskCard's -- lives in ui/main_window.py (:162, :262),
# which this change must not touch (another change owns it at the time of
# writing). Converting Shopping and the Overlay alone would put a Lucide
# circle on a shopping row and a text "○" on the task row directly above
# it: the app would be LESS consistent after the wave than before it. So
# the toggle moves as one unit, in the wave that can reach main_window.
# What that wave needs: unchecked -> `circle` (fg.muted), completed ->
# `check` (ok). The QSS rules involved are #checkButton / #OverlayCheckBtn,
# whose `color:` stops applying once the glyph is a rendered SVG -- the
# token has to move into the icons.set_icon() call, exactly as the four
# #Progress*Icon labels in ui/pages/tasks_page.py already did here.
ui/widgets/shopping_card.py:123  # completion toggle — moves with TaskCard (ui/main_window.py:162)
ui/widgets/shopping_card.py:246  # completion toggle — moves with TaskCard (ui/main_window.py:262)
ui/overlay/overlay_window.py:170  # completion toggle — moves with TaskCard (ui/main_window.py:162)
ui/overlay/overlay_window.py:201  # completion toggle — moves with TaskCard (ui/main_window.py:162)
ui/overlay/overlay_window.py:264  # completion toggle — moves with TaskCard (ui/main_window.py:162)
#
# ── 2. Colour swatches, not icons ───────────────────────────────────────
# A "●" whose whole job is to be a COLOUR is not an emoji standing in for
# an icon -- it is the cheapest possible colour swatch, and its hue comes
# from data (a custom timer's own colour, MASTER §4-4) or from a QSS
# [status=…] rule (the Flow guide's node state). A Lucide `circle` is a
# 2 px-stroked ring, not a filled disc: swapping it in would either lose
# the fill that carries the meaning, or need a `circle` + `circle-filled`
# pair that Lucide does not ship. Review D/m4 ("colour dots need a shape
# too") is a real finding and is NOT closed by this wave: closing it means
# four distinct SHAPES per status, which is a design decision for the Flow
# legend, not an icon substitution. Logged here so it cannot be forgotten.
ui/overlay/overlay_window.py:505  # live dot — colour swatch (#OverlayLiveDot), not an icon
ui/custom_timer_manager_dialog.py:117  # category marker — colour swatch (#ctCategoryDot)
ui/custom_timer_manager_dialog.py:285  # the timer's OWN colour (data colour, MASTER §4-4)
ui/flow/flow_debug.py:133  # debug overlay colour swatch, never shipped to a user
ui/flow/widgets/flow_guide_view.py:270  # node-status swatch (#GuideInfoIcon[status=…]) — review D/m4
ui/flow/widgets/flow_guide_view.py:380  # node-status swatch (#GuideInfoIcon[status=…]) — review D/m4
#
# ── 3. User data ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The Flow node symbol is CHOSEN BY THE USER from #FlowSymbolCombo and
# stored in the map. "☆" is this field's default value, not an icon the
# design system picked -- replacing it would silently rewrite user data.
ui/flow/widgets/flow_node_card.py:77  # user-chosen node symbol (default value), not a UI icon
